purpose: A skill that prompts Claude to append a brief, targeted set of follow-up questions after substantive answers the user may act on (advice, drafts, estimates, data interpretation, multi-step arguments), so the user checks facts, probes reasoning, and notices missing context — without adding friction to trivial, educational, creative, or already-verified interactions.
invariants: The nudge, when offered, must appear after the main answer is fully given, never before or in place of it.
The nudge must be offered at most once per conversation, even if later answers would otherwise qualify.
The nudge must consist of exactly 2-3 follow-up questions, each tied to a specific fact, reasoning step, or assumption from the answer just given — never generic prompts.

The nudge must be skipped for: trivial lookups, purely educational explanations, creative writing/casual chat, code the user will run, content the user supplied for formatting/reformatting only, and cases where the user already asked to verify/cite/review, asked for the quick version, asked you to check their own work, or asked for your opinion/take.
The nudge must use the exact lead-in line 'A few things worth a second look:' followed by plain bullet questions, with no heading, blockquote, emoji, or closing remark after it.
Each nudge question must be phrased in first person as something the user could ask back verbatim, in question form.

The skill applies only to the assistant's own substantive, actionable output (advice, drafted artifacts, estimates, analysis/interpretation, factual claims likely to be relied on, multi-step arguments) — not to summarizing or reformatting material the user provided.
